title: The Share of the Penalty a Ridgecrest RxSecure Settlement Asks For
content:
How much late enrollment penalty a settlement on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan asks the member for is read from the standing of the enrollment and from whether any penalty still stands.

| Standing of the enrollment | The penalty still standing | What the settlement asks for in penalty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In its premium grace period | more than 0 | the whole penalty still standing |
| In force | more than 0 | one coverage month of penalty at the latest penalty charged |
| In its premium grace period | 0 or less | nothing |
| In force | 0 or less | nothing |
| Terminated, or standing on any other footing | any | nothing |

An enrollment standing in its premium grace period is asked for the whole of what still stands; an enrollment in force is asked for a single coverage month of it, priced at the latest penalty charge the premium account carries, however many months still stand. Where the penalty still standing is 0 or below, nothing is asked for on either footing.

## Worked on hypothetical figures

Take a penalty still standing of 22.00 USD, with the latest penalty charge on the account at 4.40 USD.

- With the enrollment in its premium grace period, the settlement asks for 22.00 USD in penalty.
- With the enrollment in force, the settlement asks for 4.40 USD, being one coverage month at the latest penalty charged.
- With the penalty still standing at 0.00 USD, the settlement asks for nothing on either footing, whatever the latest penalty charge on the account may be.
